methods.name: _overview
methods.summary: Whether Docker can be reached, how the web server's container is doing, and the settings and sites it is made from. A Docker that cannot be reached is an answer (`engine.reachable` is false and says why), not an error.

methods.name: _connect
methods.summary: Choose the Docker the server runs in, and answer with what is there. A server left running in the Docker chosen before is not touched. The folders of the sites are folders of the machine that Docker runs on.

params.name: host
params.description: Where Docker listens: `unix:///path/docker.sock`, `tcp://host:2375` or `http://host:2375`. Empty for this machine's own Docker.

errors.message: The address is not one Docker can be reached at.

methods.name: _apply
methods.summary: Make the container again from the settings and the sites as they stand, and start it: the way out when it is not running, or was made from older ones. Does nothing while no site is on.

methods.name: _save_settings
methods.summary: Change the port that the sites with names share. A server that is running is made again with it.

params.name: port
params.description: The port of the machine Docker runs on that every site with a name answers on. The web's own is 80.

errors.message: The port is the own port of one of the sites: the message says which.

methods.name: _create_site
methods.summary: Host a folder as a site, on a port of its own, under names on the shared port, or both. It is on from the start, and the server is made again with it.

params.name: name
params.description: What the site is called in the list.

params.name: folder
params.description: The folder the site's files are in, as a full path on the machine Docker runs on, like `/Users/me/Sites/blog`. Its `index.html` is the front page. It is only read.

params.name: port
params.description: A port of its own for the site, like 8081. 0 for none: the site then needs a name.

params.name: hostnames
params.description: The names the site answers to on the shared port, like `blog.home`: letters, digits and hyphens, in parts joined by dots. None: the site then needs a port.

errors.message: The name, the folder, the port or a hostname cannot be used, or there are too many sites: the message says which and why.

methods.name: _update_site
methods.summary: Change a site: what it is called, its folder, its port and its names. Whether it is on stays. The server is made again with it.

params.name: site
params.description: The id of one of the sites of `overview`.

errors.message: There is no such site, or the name, the folder, the port or a hostname cannot be used: the message says which and why.

methods.name: _set_site_enabled
methods.summary: Turn a site on (it is served) or off (it is kept, and not served). With the last site off the container is removed. What Docker refused is said by `server.problem` of the answer.

params.name: site
params.description: The id of one of the sites of `overview`.

methods.name: _delete_site
methods.summary: Stop hosting a site and forget it. Its folder and the files in it are not touched.

params.name: site
params.description: The id of one of the sites of `overview`.

methods.name: _logs
methods.summary: The end of what the server has written: how it started, what it could not do, and every request it answered.

params.name: tail
params.description: How many lines from the end; 200 when left out.

errors.message: Docker cannot be reached, or the server has no container: the message says which.

methods.name: list_sites
methods.description: The websites this machine hosts, each a folder of files: its name, the folder, its own port (0 when it has none), the hostnames it answers to on the shared port, whether it is on (`enabled`), and why it is not served when its folder is missing (`problem`). Also how the web server is doing: the state of its container (`running`, `stopped`, `restarting`, or `absent` when there is none, as with every site off), the port the sites with hostnames share (`sharedPort`), and why it is not running when Docker refused (`problem`).

methods.name: add_site
methods.description: Serve a folder of this machine as a website: its `index.html` is the front page, and its files are only read. Give it a port of its own (`http://<machine>:8081`), hostnames it answers to on the shared port (`http://blog.home`, which must resolve to this machine), or both. It is served a moment later.

params.name: name
params.description: What the site is called in the list

params.name: folder
params.description: The full path of the folder, like `/Users/me/Sites/blog`

params.name: port
params.description: A port of its own, like 8081; none when left out

params.name: hostnames
params.description: Names it answers to on the shared port, like `blog.home`; none when left out

methods.name: remove_site
methods.description: Stop serving a site and forget it, by its name as `list_sites` gives it. Its folder and the files in it are not touched.

methods.name: changed
methods.summary: The server changed (Docker's events for its container, a change of the configuration): the open windows read the overview again.

version.description: Docker's version, empty when it cannot be reached.

host.description: Where Docker is looked for, as given to `connect`. Empty for this machine's own Docker.

problem.description: Why Docker cannot be reached, as a sentence. Empty when it can.

ServerState.description: How the server's container is doing: there is none, it runs, Docker is starting it again, or it is there and not running.

wanted.description: At least one site is on, so the server is wanted running. Whether it is running is `state`.

status.description: Docker's own words for the container: `Up 2 hours`, `Exited (1) 5 seconds ago`. Empty without one.

current.description: The container was made from the settings and the sites as they stand. False without one.

image.description: The image the container is made from.

problem.description: Why the container could not be made or started the last time it was tried, as a sentence. Empty when it could.

port.description: The port every site with a name answers on.

name.description: What the site is called in the list.

folder.description: The full path of the folder the site's files are in.

port.description: The site's own port; 0 when it has none.

hostnames.description: The names the site answers to on the shared port, in lower case.

problem.description: Why a site that is on is not served, as a sentence: its folder is not there. Empty when nothing is known to be wrong.

truncated.description: The text is the end of something longer.

Brief.description: How the web server is doing, as an agent reads it.

Hosted.description: A site as an agent reads it in a list.
